name: Kirchdorf in Tirol
kurzbeschreibung: Idyllic Leukental community at the foot of the Wilder Kaiser featuring the Kaiserbachtal nature reserve, Teufelsgasse, and Kaiserquell spa.
beschreibung:
Overview

Kirchdorf in Tirol is situated at an elevation of 641 metres in the sunny Leukental valley within the district of Kitzbühel. This idyllic community of around 4,150 residents lies at the dramatic southern foot of the Wilder Kaiser mountain range, just a few kilometres north of St. Johann in Tirol. Beyond the central village, the municipal area encompasses charming hamlets including Erpfendorf and Gasteig, alongside the threshold to the Kaiserbachtal Nature Reserve. Kirchdorf stands out for its serene natural scenery, extensive winter walking and cross-country ski trails, and outstanding spa amenities. Blending untouched alpine wilderness, authentic agricultural roots, and family-oriented recreation, Kirchdorf provides a haven of mountain relaxation away from busy tourist crowds.

History

Human habitation in the Leukental reaches back into antiquity, when ancient routes threaded through the valley. Kirchdorf was first documented in 1118 under the name 'Chirchdorf'. It stood among the founding mother parishes of the valley, historically serving surrounding villages. During the Tyrolean Rebellion of 1809, the town attained fame through Rupert Wintersteller, a local innkeeper and daring major who led the Leukental riflemen in successful skirmishes against Bavarian and French invaders. A showcase of traditional vernacular architecture is the Metzgerhaus dating from 1570, a heritage-listed single-roof farmstead housing an authentic local museum. The Neoclassical Parish Church of Saint Stephen, constructed between 1815 and 1818, impresses with its stately proportions and ceiling frescoes painted by the celebrated master Josef Schöpf.

Getting There

Arriving by car is straightforward via the Inntal Autobahn A12 to Kufstein-Süd, continuing toll-free along the B173 and B178 via Ellmau to St. Johann in Tirol, where the B176 Kössener Federal Highway leads directly to Kirchdorf. Driving from Munich or Salzburg, motorists take the A8 Autobahn to Siegsdorf/Inzell and proceed via Lofer and Waidring. Rail travellers arrive at the St. Johann in Tirol railway station, served frequently by ÖBB InterCity and regional services. Directly outside the terminal, VVT regional buses heading toward Kössen and Waidring stop regularly throughout Kirchdorf, Erpfendorf, and the Kaiserbachtal.

Tips

An essential destination is the pristine Kaiserbachtal Nature Reserve beneath the jagged limestone spires of the Wilder Kaiser. A gentle toll road leads past the Fischbachalm to the Griesner Alm at 1,024 metres, the starting point for classic hikes up to the Stripsenjochhaus; near the valley entrance, the historic Hofmann Mountain Pine Oil Distillery from 1933 illustrates the production of aromatic alpine remedies. Another thrilling excursion is exploring the Teufelsgasse on the Leerberg ridge, a mythical rock labyrinth featuring narrow chasms and mossy fissures. For post-hike relaxation, the Kaiserquell wellness resort offers indoor and outdoor pools, saunas, and tennis. In winter, cross-country skiers can glide over 80 kilometres of meticulously groomed tracks throughout the Koasa region.
